title: Fidelity report finds Solana resilient but flags concentration in stake, hosting and clients
summary:
Solana's resilience is notable, but its stake concentration poses systemic risks, potentially impacting network stability and decentralization.
The post Fidelity report finds Solana resilient but flags concentration in stake, hosting and clients appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: A recent Fidelity report highlights Solana's overall network resilience while raising concerns over centralization risks. The report points to high concentration levels in staking, hosting providers, and client software, which could pose systemic challenges to the blockchain's long-term stability and decentralization.

title: TokenMaxxing: How to Get the Most Out of Your AI Models
summary: AI companies charge by the token, and most people burn them on jobs a cheap model could do. Here's how to spend less and get better results, from your first prompt to your first agent.
content: AI companies charge users by the token, leading many to waste resources on tasks that less expensive models could handle efficiently. By optimizing prompt strategies and using appropriate models for different tasks, users can significantly reduce costs and improve their overall results, whether working with simple prompts or building advanced AI agents.
content_ta: AI நிறுவனங்கள் token அடிப்படையிலேயே கட்டணம் வசூலிக்கின்றன. இதனால் பலர் எளிய மாடல்களால் செய்யக்கூடிய பணிகளுக்காக அதிக வளங்களை வீணடிக்கின்றனர். ப்ராம்ப்ட் உத்திகளை மேம்படுத்துவதன் மூலமாகவும், பணிகளுக்கு ஏற்ற மாடல்களைத் தேர்ந்தெடுப்பதன் மூலமாகவும் செலவைக் குறைத்து சிறந்த பலன்களைப் பெற முடியும்.

title: UK Businesses File £700m CAT Claim over Visa and Mastercard EEA Fees
summary:
A Competition Appeal Tribunal claim alleges the card networks raised UK-EEA interchange fees five-fold after Brexit, costing businesses up to £200m a year.
The post UK Businesses File £700m CAT Claim over Visa and Mastercard EEA Fees appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: UK businesses have filed a £700m claim with the Competition Appeal Tribunal against Visa and Mastercard. The lawsuit alleges that the major card networks increased UK-EEA interchange fees significantly following Brexit, resulting in substantial annual costs for affected companies.

Brexit-க்குப் பிறகு கார்டு நெட்வொர்க்குகள் கட்டணங்களை உயர்த்தியதால் நிறுவனங்களுக்கு ஆண்டுதோறும் பெரும் இழப்பு ஏற்பட்டுள்ளதாகக் கூறப்படுகிறது.

title: Solana shows resilience, but some areas need continued observation, Fidelity says
summary: Solana has had no reported mainnet outages in two years, but concentrations in stake, hosting and client software should be monitored, according to a report.
content: A recent report by Fidelity highlights the resilience of the Solana network, noting it has experienced no reported mainnet outages in two years. However, the report cautions that certain areas, including concentrations in stake, hosting, and client software, require continued observation and monitoring.

title: Only 10.7% of tokenized stock market cap is issuer-sponsored
summary:
The dominance of synthetic tokens over issuer-sponsored ones highlights potential risks in investor rights and market dependency on custodians.
The post Only 10.7% of tokenized stock market cap is issuer-sponsored appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: A recent report reveals that only 10.7 percent of the total tokenized stock market capitalization is issuer-sponsored. The heavy reliance on synthetic tokens instead of issuer-backed assets raises potential concerns regarding investor rights and the overall market's dependency on custodians.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $82 Million As BlackRock Leads Friday’s Withdrawals
summary: TL;DR: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $82.4 million in net outflows on October 16. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $71.8 million of withdrawals, with Fidelity’s FBTC recording about $10.6 million. BlackRock’s flagship spot Bitcoin ETF accounted for most of the selling as US-listed Bitcoin investment funds closed Friday’s session with net withdrawals of approximately $82.4 million. Farside Investors’ figures show that the iShares Bitcoin Trust, known as IBIT, lost $71.8 million on October 16. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund recorded around $10.6 million in net outflows, while the remaining products were broadly flat on the day. That concentration matters because IBIT has become one of the clearest measures of Bitcoin demand through traditional brokerage accounts. Another Uneven Week For ETF Demand The latest withdrawals followed substantial redemptions earlier in the week. October 14 saw roughly $261 million leave the category, followed by a modest return to net inflows on October 15. Friday’s negative session therefore suggests demand remains unsettled rather than following a clear trend. Investors have seen considerably larger individual outflow days in the past. Earlier October withdrawals approached $485 million in a single session, demonstrating how rapidly demand through these products can shift. Context Is Important An ETF outflow is not a complete measure of institutional Bitcoin ownership, and it does not necessarily indicate that every underlying holder has abandoned a long-term position. Net inflows into the US spot Bitcoin ETF market since the products launched remained substantial despite the latest withdrawals. The next trading sessions will be important. A quick recovery would suggest another temporary adjustment, while continued redemptions from IBIT and FBTC would place greater emphasis on whether traditional investors are reducing their exposure amid broader market uncertainty. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $82 million in net outflows. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for the majority of the withdrawals with $71.8 million, while Fidelity’s FBTC recorded about $10.6 million. This follows a volatile week for ETF demand, highlighting ongoing shifts in traditional market interest amid broader economic uncertainty.
